title: Black Sun (Le Soleil Noir)
description: Black Sun (Le Soleil Noir) signed and dated 'S.H. RAZA, '53.' (lower left); further signed, dated, titled and inscribed 'RAZA / 1953 / "Black Sun" / 46 x 48 cms' (on the reverse) gouache on paper 18 ¼ x 18 7⁄8 in. (46.4 x 47.9 cm.) Executed in 1953
provenance: Galerie Raymond Creuze, ParisAcquired from the above by Mr and Mrs Jacques Lassaigne, June 1953 Thence by descentAfter studying law and working as a journalist at Le Figaro, Jacques Lassaigne published his first book on the artist Honoré Daumier in 1937. Today, Lassaigne is remembered as a prominent critic and curator who authored several books on art movements and artists, including monographs on Van Gogh, Kandinsky, Miro and Chagall. Lassaigne also served as President of the International Association of Art Critics and Chief Curator of the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville in Paris. Following his retirement, he was appointed artistic adviser to the city of Paris, a position he held till his death in 1983.

title: Untitled (Tree and Woman)
description: Untitled (Tree and Woman) faintly inscribed 'To Martin / in friendship' (on the reverse) etching on paper 13 ¼ x 19 ¾ in. (33.7 x 50.2 cm.) image; 16 ½ x 23 3⁄8 in. (41.9 x 59.4 cm.) sheet Executed circa late 1960s
provenance: Gifted by the artist to Martin Hewitt, August 1969Private British CollectionAcquired from the aboveMartin Hewitt was an English architect and close friend of the artist Gulammohammed Sheikh. They met when Sheikh was was studying at the Royal College of Art (RCA) in London on a Commonwealth scholarship in the mid-1960s. During Sheikh's third and last year in the city, he shared a basement flat in Addison Gardens, West London, with Hewitt and two other architects, Shreeram Marathe and David Cocherane. Interestingly, one of the works Sheikh exhibited at his RCA Examination Show that year was a portrait of Hewitt (Composition in Green and Black, 1966). After Sheikh's return to India, Hewitt visited him there in 1968, designing the sets for the production of 'Blood Wedding' at the Faculty of Fine Arts of M.S. University in Baroda that Sheikh directed that year, and documenting his life and work along with that of close friends like Bhupen Khakhar in a series of photographs.

provenance: Acquired directly from the artist by Vernon W. Ruttan, circa early 1960sThence by descentVernon W. Ruttan (1924–2008) was a development economist whose research focused on agriculture, technical innovation and productivity. Over the course of a distinguished career, he served on the President's Council of Economic Advisors, the Rockefeller Foundation at the International Rice Research Institute in the Philippines, and as President of the Agricultural Development Council. He was a member of the National Academy of Sciences and, from 1986, was Regents' Professor in the department of Applied Economics at the University of Minnesota. His interest in modern art and design was shared by his wife, and they collected works by artists they met and interacted with over the course of their travels across the world, including in India and the Philippines.

provenance: The Collection of Dr Lal Jayawardena and Dr Kumari Jayawardena Acquired from the above by the present owner, 2001 Dr Lal R. Jayawardena (1935–2004) was a well-known economist and diplomat who held several posts with the Sri Lankan government from the 1970s onwards. After serving as the Sri Lankan Treasury Secretary in the 1970s, he was appointed the country's Ambassador to Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands from 1978–82, and High Commissioner to the United Kingdom and Ireland from 1999–2000. In between, he led the World Institute for Development Economics Research, served as Economic Adviser to the Sri Lankan President and as Deputy Chairman of the Sri Lankan National Development Council. Dr Kumari Jayawardena (B. 1931) is a noted academic and activist, whose book Feminism and Nationalism in the Third World is considered part of the canon of global feminist studies and is taught worldwide. She has held teaching posts at the University of Colombo and the International Institute of Social Studies in the Hague and continues to play an important role in various women's and civil rights groups in Sri Lanka.

title: Untitled (Still Life)
description: Untitled (Still Life) signed and dated 'G Keyt 52' (upper right) oil on canvas 24 x 30 3⁄8 in. (61 x 77.1 cm.) Painted in 1952
provenance: Gifted by the artist to Pararajasingam Nadesan, Colombo, 1952Thence by descentAcquired from the above by the present owner, 2001Pararajasingam 'Park' Nadesan, OBE, CMG, joined the Ceylon Civil Service in 1941 following his studies at the Royal College Colombo and University of London. After serving as cadet, additional magistrate and additional deputy controller in several districts, he was appointed Director of Civil Aviation and secretary to Prime Minister Sir John Kotelawala till he retired in 1956. Nadesan was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire in 1954, and a Companion of the Order of St Michael and St George the following year. In the early 1950s, George Keyt lived in Nadesan's home in Colombo and gifted him this painting in gratitude.
